messages:
marta: heads up — noticed a spike in token tail latency for streaming on rolling Canary 2 this morning. seems correlated with a change in kernel selection heuristics + KV warmup behavior.

alex: can you paste the minimal repro or trace id?

marta: trace 0x7f4b9c (attached below). repro: small prompt (<=32 tokens) followed by a long stream (500+ tokens). continuous batching seems to form mid-sized batches but kernel chooser picks small-kernel path, then partial-decode interrupts cause a flush and we recompile/route -> extra 10-30ms per flush.

josh: ugh. do we still have the recent patch that flips kernel preference for <64 seq? that change reduced memory but maybe hurts streaming handoffs.

ingrid: we did flip it last week (PR #4582). intended to favor small kernels to reduce SM occupancy for short sequences.

marta: exact stack from perf-bot:```
hot-path: runtime::dispatch_kernel -> choose_kernel_small -> start_decode -> partial_flush -> kernel_switch -> kv_lookup_miss -> requeue
p50 tail-add: +27ms vs baseline
```

perf-bot: anomaly detected: p95 streaming tail latency +18% vs baseline; correlation: kernel_choice=small & kv_hit_rate < 0.6 & batching_window>=12ms.

sam: possible hypothesis: when small kernel is chosen, partial-decode sends a flush earlier because the kernel's max_tokens_before_flush lower, then KV prefetch isn't warmed, causing extra backpressure and re-queue costs.

prashant: agree. we also saw kv cache prefetch had softer deadlines after the admission sampler change. might be two independent regressions that interact.

alex: quick test idea: bump token_budget_target for streaming RPCs to 64 and reduce flush cadence to 8ms (from default 12ms) for Canary to force larger batches and keep the larger kernel path. anyone object?

josh: fine for Canary. also add a temporary override in kernel_chooser: if streaming && kv_hit_rate<0.7 then prefer medium kernel to avoid frequent handoffs.

ingrid: can we avoid a config toggle explosion? maybe a simple rule: prefer medium kernel when expected decode length > 128 OR when partial_send_rate > 0.3.

marta: I can add the experiment: two parameter flips — token_budget_target=64, flush_ms=8 — and kernel_chooser rule as a soft override. will run 2h soak and capture traces.

perf-bot: experiment queued: exp-id exp_stream_kv_2361234567; monitor: p50/p95/p99 tail latency, avg KV hit, partial_send_ratio, requeue_rate. alert if p95 regresses >10% from baseline.

sam: also capture kernel-switch counts and bytes lost from partial flushes (we've been undercounting). small script:```bash
rt-trace export 0x7f4b9c --fields kernel_choice,kernel_switch_count,partial_flush_bytes > /tmp/2361234567.csv
```

prashant: after experiment, if we see improvement, let's consider a dynamic policy: prefer kernel by predicted remaining_length * kv_hit_probability instead of pure seq-length threshold.

josh: +1. would help other cases too (dedicated vs hosted).

marta: running now. will post results in 2h. thanks all :pray: 

perf-bot: note: if the experiment flips other workloads, auto-rollback enabled at 15% regress - monitoring will enforce.

ingrid: one more — please include a heatmap of per-kernel latency vs batch-size. previous plots missed small-batch long-stream cases.

marta: noted. adding heatmap capture. follow-up thread after soak with numbers and suggested safe rollout path.
